summary: The subset defines strong fail-closed scanner, exploration, artifact, and verification contracts, but two security-boundary defects block PASS: artifact readers are launched through ambient Python resolution, and Playwright's claimed residual-credential check is only an idempotence check.

findings.title: Artifact reader uses ambient Python resolution
findings.evidence: The prescribed pre-trust artifact-reading command starts with unqualified `python3`, so an activated project-local environment or project-containing PATH can select target-controlled executable code before the bundled reader validates the artifact.
findings.recommendation: Provide and prescribe a bundled launcher that binds and validates an absolute non-project Python interpreter under an isolated environment; use the same boundary for Cypress readers.

findings.title: Residual credential check is ineffective
findings.evidence: After assigning `value = redact_sensitive(value)`, the code only compares a second application of the same sanitizer with the first result. Any credential shape missed by the sanitizer remains unchanged and therefore passes this check, contrary to the documented fail-closed residual-credential guarantee.
findings.recommendation: After redaction, run independent residual credential detectors over every emitted string and fail when any supported authorization, cookie, assignment, URL-userinfo, or query-secret shape remains.

limitations: Packet-only static review; no files outside the frozen subset were considered and no commands or runtime probes were executed.
Omitted tests, holdouts, benchmark evidence, referenced helper files, host behavior, installation success, and actual framework versions were not evaluated.
This is not full product coverage, skill-accuracy evidence, independent ground truth, or remote model attestation.
